title: NimbleBrain catalog-entry extension
description: The `ai.nimblebrain` entry of an AI Catalog entry's `extensions`: what a NimbleBrain host shows and gates a listed item on without opening its artifact. A listing selects what installs (the entry's `url`, `digest` or inline `data`); what an install produces comes only from the verified artifact, so nothing here is read at install or grants anything. A plugin manifest's `extensions["ai.nimblebrain"]` has its own schema (plugin-extension/v1). Readers ignore fields they do not know.

iconUrl.description: An http(s) URL of the item's icon, shown where the item is listed.

category.description: The category the item is listed under, as display text, e.g. "Sales & CRM".

servers.description: The item's servers, by server key (the key the artifact uses for the server): each one's registry name and auth. It describes what the artifact holds so the listing can be read without it; an install reads the servers from the verified artifact, never from here.

^(.*)$.description: One server the listed item connects: its registry name and how it signs in.

auth.description: How the server signs in, so a host can say what an install will ask for: `dcr` (the host registers its own OAuth client), `none`, `static` (an OAuth client the operator registers first), `provider` (a credential the host mints), or the id of the broker that holds the session (e.g. `composio`), which only a host that has that broker can install.

nimblebrainOnly.description: True when only NimbleBrain can run the item: a server it names is brokered, or needs an operator's own OAuth app. It describes the item; it grants nothing.
